blocks.text: The week in wildlife: a penguin posse, a little leopard cat and a chonky squirrel
This week’s best wildlife photographs from around the world

blocks.alt: Wily Coyotes of San Francisco by Loren Elliott, one of the winners of the Wildlife photographer of the year award. Elliott opens a window into the lives of the often-misunderstood coyotes living in the environs of San Francisco. About 100 of these urban-adapted wild canines live alongside more than 800,000 human inhabitants, and attitudes towards them are mixed. Coyotes sometimes prey on domestic animals, but they also bring benefits such as controlling disease-carrying rodents

blocks.alt: ‘Xiaosonguo’, a leopard cat under second-class state protection, is released into a wildlife habitat in Dongguan, Guangdong Province of China. The animal was found and rescued in April by the Dongguan Forestry Bureau before being transferred to the Qingyuan Chimelong Wildlife Rescue Centre
An American Barn Owl sits perched on a water tower in Manhattan, New York City, US

A red deer stag bellows at sunrise during the annual rut in Richmond Park, London, UK. The park is home to hundreds of red and fallow deer, with the autumn rut marking the breeding season when stags bellow, clash antlers and compete for access to females

A western gray squirrel peels the husk from a black walnut while foraging beneath a tree near the Umpqua River in southwestern Oregon, US. Native to the western United States, the squirrels feed on nuts, seeds and other plant material, often burying nuts in scattered locations to store food for winter

A rare Hummingbird hawkmoth photographed in full flight, UK. The moth is a summer visitor to the UK from southern Europe and North Africa but can be seen in most months of the year. With warmer summers it now breeds in the UK and will often overwinter here and can now be considered a UK breeding species. It beats its wings so fast, up to 90 beats a second, that they emit an audible hum – hence the name and its similarity to Hummingbirds. It means that it can manoeuvre easily with its long proboscis able to delve into deeper flower stems such as red valerian

Wild elephants break through electric fences to enter villages near Ambanpola, Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka’s forest cover has plummeted from roughly 70% in the 1920s to about 34% today and as many as 70% of Sri Lanka’s estimated 7,451 wild elephants live outside protected areas

A rare cao vit gibbon. A recent survey by Fauna & Flora, local rangers, and community members indicates that the population of the rare cao vit gibbon—found only in a small forest bordering Vietnam and China—has grown to approximately 77–89 individuals.
A praying mantis, commonly found in tropical and subtropical regions, is seen in Sirataslar Valley at an altitude of 2,000m Sarikamis district of Kars, Turkey
Bali Marine Police officers release green sea turtles at a beach in Serangan, Bali, Indonesia. Police seized and released 20 green sea turtles from illegal poachers
An orangutan rescued from wildfires is released into a protected forest in Batu Nyambu, West Kalimantan, Indonesia

Thirteen rescued freshwater turtles are returned to the Gingham water hole in New South Wales, Australia, after environmental water flows were restored, six months after their habitat dried up. Thirty-nine turtles were rescued and now the first group of 13 surviving turtles have been returned to their habitat

blocks.text: freshwater turtle is one of 13 that are being returned to their home, the Gingham water hole in New South Wales, Australia, which dried up after the water company cut flows to the area. After a public outcry, the utility reversed its decision, and 24 more turtles will soon follow the first group of 13 back to their restored habitatPhotograph: NSW Government

blocks.alt: Swans sit at the beach of Travemuende, Germany

A mountain gazelle trots along the Syrian border between Kirikhan and Kumlu districts in Hatay, Turkey. The region, which is home to a large portion of the world’s mountain gazelle population and represents the species’ northernmost habitat, is seeing an increase in the population of the endangered species thanks to conservation projects

Cranes feed on a harvested field near Balmazujvaros, northeastern Hungary. During their autumn migration, tens of thousands of cranes gather on the Hortobagy steppe to forage in the surrounding agricultural areas during daytime

A clouded yellow butterfly feeds on a yellow wildflower in Diyarbakir, southeastern Turkey. The butterfly’s yellow-green wings blend subtly with the surrounding vegetation, while its feeding behavior highlights the ecological role of pollinating insects in natural habitats
A cormorant and a heron search for fish together in a wetland in Nagaon District, Assam, India

A blue crab blows bubbles of air and water from its mouthparts as on the beach at Isle of Palms, South Carolina, US. Crabs out of water push air across their gills, forming bubbles that help keep the gills moist

Gentoo penguins on Pebble Island, Falklands Islands. Gentoo penguins, along with five different penguin species, as well as over 40 other bird species can be found on Pebble Island, situated just off the north coast of West Falkland. It is an important wildlife sanctuary hosting breeding colonies. Gentoo penguins breeding activity begins in late September, with peak egg laying occurring by mid-October
